scenarios.title: Cross-tenant authorization
scenarios.claim: An operator can act on their own tenants and on nothing else; a deployment webhook changes a deployment only forward and only once.
scenarios.method: The real server actions, API routes and deploy logic against a migrated Postgres (PGlite). Only the session, GitHub dispatch and the tenant's signer and backend are replaced, each recording what it was asked to do; the database is read back after every operation.

scenarios.title: Cloud identity isolation
scenarios.claim: A run for tenant A can sign in to A's cloud and fetch A's secrets, and cannot do either for tenant B.
scenarios.method: Simulated STS and Entra ID decisions against the bootstrap templates, with forged token claims; the platform's own secrets release run for real against PGlite with AES-GCM ciphertexts and locally signed RS256 tokens.

scenarios.claim: Dispatch inputs are only data: they cannot run a command or rewrite another step's output.
scenarios.method: The workflows' own step scripts executed in local bash with GitHub's flags and $GITHUB_OUTPUT semantics; aws, docker, az, terraform and curl stubbed to record their arguments; a canary file detects code execution.
